sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in Bellevue, WA?
sections.html:
Bellevue is a high-value market: the Census Bureau puts the median value of an owner-occupied home at $1,340,300 for 2020 to 2024, and estimates 154,193 residents as of July 1, 2025. About 52.0% of housing is owner-occupied, median household income is $165,576, and median gross rent is $2,572.

The population is diverse and highly educated: 43.5% of residents were born outside the United States, 48.8% of those age five and older speak a language other than English at home, and 72.1% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher. The average commute is 23.6 minutes. The city covers 37.5 square miles of land and water combined and had 151,854 residents at the 2020 census, up from 122,363 in 2010.

sections.h2: Where is Bellevue, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Bellevue is an Eastside city in King County, across Lake Washington from Seattle and between that lake and Lake Sammamish. Interstate 405 runs through it north to south, Interstate 90 crosses the southern part, and State Route 520 roughly marks the northern edge. Kirkland and Redmond sit to the north, Issaquah to the east, Mercer Island across the East Channel Bridge, and Newcastle and Renton to the south. South of I-90 the city climbs Cougar Mountain.

William Meydenbauer and Aaron Mercer claimed homesteads here in 1869, and permanent residents arrived around 1879. Logging came first, and Japanese immigrant labor later cleared much of the land for small farms. The Bellevue Strawberry Festival began in 1925. The Lake Washington Floating Bridge opened in 1940 and the Evergreen Point Floating Bridge in 1963, and the second bridge set off faster growth. Bellevue incorporated on March 31, 1953, annexed Crossroads in 1964 and Lake Hills in 1969, and by the 1970 census was the fourth most populous city in the state.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and school districts matter to Bellevue buyers?
sections.html:
The city names fourteen neighborhoods, and the list below groups them for easier reading.

  • Downtown, Wilburton/BelRed and Eastgate/Factoria.
  • Bridle Trails, Northwest Bellevue, Northeast Bellevue and West Bellevue.
  • Crossroads, Lake Hills, Newport and Somerset.
  • Cougar Mountain/Lakemont, Woodridge and West Lake Sammamish.

The vast majority of the city is served by the Bellevue School District, whose main public high schools are Bellevue High, Interlake, Newport and Sammamish, with International School and Big Picture School as choice programs. Portions of the city lie in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah school districts, so check the district for your address. Bellevue College is in the city, as are several independent schools such as Bellevue Christian School and Open Window School.

sections.h2: How do jobs and light rail affect Bellevue home values?
sections.html:
Employment is the engine. According to the city's 2024 financial report, Amazon is the largest employer with 14,300 workers, followed by T-Mobile (7,800), Meta (5,400), Overlake Hospital Medical Center (3,800) and the Bellevue School District (2,900). Downtown Bellevue is the second largest city center in Washington, with about 1,300 businesses, 45,000 employees and 10,200 residents.

Transit has caught up with the jobs. Sound Transit's 2 Line runs from Lynnwood to Redmond through Seattle, Mercer Island and Bellevue. The first section, South Bellevue to Redmond Technology station, opened April 27, 2024, and the Seattle to Bellevue section opened in March 2026. The Bellevue Transit Center downtown serves both King County Metro and Sound Transit buses, and a fare-free electric shuttle run by Circuit began operating in August 2023.

The weather is typical Puget Sound. Bellevue averages about 32 inches of rain a year, with frequent showers from October to May, though 2016 reached 47.14 inches. Highs in July and August average in the high 70s.

sections.h2: Can a Bellevue house be rented short term?
sections.html:
Usually not as a whole house. Bellevue's Land Use Code defines transient lodging as a stay of less than 30 days, and an entire single-family home or a home with an accessory dwelling unit cannot be used that way. Long-term rentals of 30 days or more are allowed, and an ADU may be rented only on a long-term basis. This matters if a buyer is counting on vacation-rental income, so state the limits clearly when you list.

Type of homeShort-term rental rule
Entire single-family home, or home with an ADUNot allowed for transient lodging.
Rooms in an owner-occupied single-family homeAllowed as a boarding house or bed and breakfast: owner-occupied, at most two rooms and two adults per room, with an approved home occupation permit (LUC 20.20.140).
Apartment, condo or planned unit development in a residential districtAllowed with a Short-Term Stay Use Registration Notice, limited to five units and 20% of the units in the development (LUC 20.20.800).

Source: City of Bellevue Residential Rental Regulations. Development Services Land Use answers questions at 425-452-4188 or landusereview@bellevuewa.gov.

sections.h2: Which work on a Bellevue house needs a permit?
sections.html:
Many common projects do. Bellevue Development Services publishes a list of work that requires permits, and these are the examples most likely to come up before a sale.

  • Additions that add square footage, including a second story or dormers, need a permit with plan review.
  • Converting a garage or carport into living space needs a permit with plan review.
  • Decks with a walking surface more than 30 inches above the ground need a permit with plan review.
  • Interior remodels that create new walls or turn a basement into living area need a permit.
  • Furnaces, heat pumps, new gas lines, new electrical circuits and EV charging stations need permits.
  • An interior accessory dwelling unit needs approval, and the review takes several weeks.

Some work needs nothing. The city does not require a permit for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops, replacing a window or door with the same size in the same spot, or building a fence under eight feet tall, though fences over 4.5 feet often cannot sit in front-yard setbacks. Emergency repairs such as a failed water heater or furnace can start first, with the permit obtained on the first city work day afterward.

sections.h2: How are taxes and closing handled when selling in Bellevue?
sections.html:
King County bills property tax on a Bellevue house. Under RCW 84.56.020 the first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31, and RCW 84.60.020 makes the tax a lien from January 1 and divides the year between seller and buyer by days when the contract is silent. Your escrow officer normally prorates the bill at closing and pays any unpaid amount from your proceeds.

Washington law also requires a seller disclosure statement for improved residential property. Under RCW 64.06.020 you must deliver it within five business days after a written contract is mutually accepted unless the buyer waived it, and the buyer has three business days after delivery to rescind.

The state real estate excise tax is usually paid by the seller and is due to the county treasurer on the date of sale. For sales beginning January 1, 2027, the rates are 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% from $551,000 to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3% above. At Bellevue's census median value of $1,340,300 the state share would be about $16,164 before the local portion, which your closing agent can confirm.

faqs.q: Can I rent my whole Bellevue house on a short-term basis?
faqs.a: No. Bellevue does not allow an entire single-family home or a home with an ADU to be used for transient lodging, which is a stay under 30 days. Long-term rentals of 30 days or more are allowed.

faqs.q: Does replacing kitchen cabinets in Bellevue need a permit?
faqs.a: A building permit is not required for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops. A plumbing or electrical permit may still be needed if that work is part of the job.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Bellevue home?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Bellevue School District, but portions are in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts. Check the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: How soon must a Bellevue seller give the buyer the disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Within five business days after both sides accept a written contract, unless the buyer waived it or the transfer is exempt. The buyer then has three business days after delivery to rescind.

faqs.q: How much state excise tax would a $1,340,300 Bellevue sale owe?
faqs.a: Under the rates for sales beginning January 1, 2027, the state portion would be about $16,164: 1.1% on the first $551,000 and 1.28% on the rest. A local portion is added.
